plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, the 4-date timeline completes: 6 Jul 1924 (Hans Berger in Jena records the first human EEG brainwaves, published 1929) · 4 Jun–6 Jul 1938 (Nathaniel Kleitman and Bruce Richardson live 32 days in Mammoth Cave, Kentucky, proving the endogenous ~24-hour human circadian rhythm) · 1952–4 Sep 1953 (Eugene Aserinsky and Nathaniel Kleitman discover Rapid Eye Movement REM dreaming sleep on 8-year-old Armond Aserinsky in Chicago; 90-minute cycle mapped with William Dement in 1957) · 2012–18 Oct 2013 (Maiken Nedergaard, Jeff Iliff, and Lulu Xie discover the glymphatic system and >60% sleep-driven expansion of brain interstitial channels in Science) alongside the 8-hour vs 6-hour sleep architecture curve showing front-loaded deep slow-wave glymphatic wash and back-loaded morning REM dream cycles.

teach_overlay.detail: Animated 4-date timeline (6 Jul 1924 → 2012–18 Oct 2013) alongside the 8-hour vs 6-hour sleep architecture curve showing front-loaded deep slow-wave glymphatic wash and back-loaded morning REM dream cycles
teach_overlay.scale: cutting your sleep from eight hours to six doesn't just lose a quarter of the night — it chops off up to two-thirds of your richest morning REM dream cycles
